extracted.intended_audience: Authors and reviewers submitting to the NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks track
extracted.subtask_short: NeurIPS 2023 Datasets & Benchmarks track submission and review criteria
extracted.subtask_description: Call for papers for the NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks track. Establishes scope, submission requirements, supplementary-material requirements, and the criteria a program committee uses to evaluate dataset and benchmark contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets should be available and accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: A key criterion is accessibility: datasets should be available and accessible, i.e. the data can be found and obtained without a personal request to the PI, and any required code should be open source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should also submit supplementary materials such as detail on how the data was collected and organized, what kind of information it contains, how it should be used ethically and responsibly, as well as how it will be made available and maintained. Open credentialized access is allowed only as an exception (e.g. ethically sensitive medical data) and must be open to a large section of the public, provide rapid response, and be guaranteed to be maintained for many years (e.g. PhysioNet Credentialing). Misuse to shield data behind a Data Transfer Agreement is grounds for desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete dataset documentation and intended uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission introducing new datasets must include the following in the supplementary materials (as a separate PDF): Dataset documentation and intended uses. Recommended documentation frameworks include datasheets for datasets, dataset nutrition labels, data statements for NLP, data cards, and accountability frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per NeurIPS ethics guidelines, datasets must be accompanied by documentation communicating the details of the dataset as part of their submissions via structured templates. Sufficient detail must be provided on how the data was collected and organized, what kind of information it contains, ethically and responsibly, and how it will be made available and maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: URL to website/platform for viewing and downloading the dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: URL to website/platform where the dataset/benchmark can be viewed and downloaded by the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links to access the dataset and its metadata can be hidden upon submission if the dataset is not yet publicly available but must be added in the camera-ready version. In select cases (e.g. when the data can only be released at a later date), this can be added afterward (up to a year after the submission deadline). Simulation environments should link to open source code repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author statement of responsibility and confirmation of data license
rubrics_metrics.description: Author statement that they bear all responsibility in case of violation of rights, etc., and confirmation of the data license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required as part of supplementary materials for any new dataset submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting, licensing, and maintenance plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosting, licensing, and maintenance plan. The choice of hosting platform is yours, as long as you ensure access to the data (possibly through a curated interface) and will provide the necessary maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Largely follows the NeurIPS guidelines for data submission but allows more freedom for non-static datasets. Long-term preservation must be clear: it must be clear that the dataset will be available for a long time, either by uploading to a data repository or by explaining how the authors themselves will ensure this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open and widely used data format with detailed reading instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset itself should ideally use an open and widely used data format. Provide a detailed explanation on how the dataset can be read. For simulation environments, use existing frameworks or explain how they can be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit license, ideally CC for datasets and open-source for code
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit license: Authors must choose a license, ideally a CC license for datasets, or an open source license for code (e.g. RL environments). An overview of licenses can be found here: https://paperswithcode.com/datasets/license
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per NeurIPS ethics guidelines, authors should provide licenses for any datasets released. These should consider the intended use and limitations of the dataset, and develop licenses and terms of use to prevent misuse or inappropriate use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured metadata using web standards (schema.org, DCAT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add structured metadata to a dataset's meta-data page using Web standards (like schema.org and DCAT): This allows it to be discovered and organized by anyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guide can be found here: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/data-types/dataset. If you use an existing data repository, this is often done automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent dereferenceable identifier (DOI) for the dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly recommended: a persistent dereferenceable identifier (e.g. a DOI minted by a data repository or a prefix on identifiers.org) for datasets, or a code repository (e.g. GitHub, GitLab,...) for code. If this is not possible or useful, please explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility of benchmark results
rubrics_metrics.description: For benchmarks, the supplementary materials must ensure that all results are easily reproducible. Where possible, use a reproducibility framework such as the ML reproducibility checklist, or otherwise guarantee that all results can be easily reproduced, i.e. all necessary datasets, code, and evaluation procedures must be accessible and documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions should be accompanied by sufficient information to reproduce the results described i.e. all necessary datasets, code, and evaluation procedures must be accessible and documented. If submissions include code, refer to the NeurIPS code submission guidelines. Reviewers will be asked: Was code provided (e.g. in the supplementary material)? If provided, did you look at the code? Did you consider it useful in guiding your review? If not provided, did you wish code had been available?

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of LLM use in methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: We expect papers to fully describe their methodology, and any tool that is important to that methodology, including the use of LLMs, should be described also. For example, authors should mention tools (including LLMs) that were used for data processing or filtering, visualization, facilitating or running experiments, and proving theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may also be advisable to describe the use of LLMs in implementing the method (if this corresponds to an important, original, or non-standard component of the approach). Authors are responsible for the entire content of the paper, including all text and figures, so while authors are welcome to use any tool they wish for writing the paper, they must ensure that all text is correct and original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility, quality, impact, originality and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility and quality of the submission: Impact, originality, novelty, relevance to the NeurIPS community will all be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the general evaluation factors that apply to all submissions in the Datasets and Benchmarks track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: address ethical implications of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics: Any ethical implications of the work should be addressed. Authors should rely on NeurIPS ethics guidelines as guidance for understanding ethical concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any ethical implications of new datasets should be addressed and guidelines for responsible use should be provided where appropriate. If your submission includes publicly available datasets (e.g. as part of a larger benchmark), you should also check these datasets for ethical issues. You remain responsible for the ethical implications of including existing datasets or other data sources in your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent and privacy for datasets with real people
rubrics_metrics.description: Consent and privacy: Per NeurIPS ethics guidelines, datasets should minimize the exposure of any personally identifiable information, unless informed consent from those individuals is provided to do so. Any paper that chooses to create a dataset with real data of real people should ask for the explicit consent of participants, or explain why they were unable to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal compliance with regional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal compliance: For datasets, authors should ensure awareness and compliance with regional legal requirements.
